name: The Solar System
description: The Sun, the planets and their moons, and how telescopes and space probes revealed them.

checkpoints.name: How the planets formed
checkpoints.note: A cloud of gas and dust collapses into the Sun and a disc of planets. Giant impacts shape the young Earth and its Moon, Ceres is left as the largest body between Mars and Jupiter, and icy Pluto, Charon and Eris circle far beyond Neptune.

checkpoints.name: Watching the sky
checkpoints.note: For thousands of years people track the five bright planets by eye and argue over whether the Earth or the Sun is at the centre, until Copernicus puts the Sun there in 1543. Early in the 1600s the telescope appears in the Netherlands.

checkpoints.name: The telescope age
checkpoints.note: Galileo turns a telescope on Jupiter and finds four moons, and Kepler's laws describe how the planets move. Astronomers find Titan and Uranus, Le Verrier predicts Neptune from its pull and then a planet Vulcan that is not there, and Pluto joins the list in 1930.

checkpoints.name: Space probes
checkpoints.note: Mariner 4 photographs Mars, Venera 7 lands on Venus and Viking reaches the Martian surface. Apollo 11 puts people on the Moon; Voyager, Galileo, Cassini and New Horizons reveal volcanoes on Io, oceans under icy moons and a heart on Pluto; the find of Eris makes Pluto a dwarf planet in 2006; and Curiosity and Chang'e 4 roam Mars and the Moon's far side.
